newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zambian govt attacks press freedom award winner.
newsitem.headline: Zambian govt attacks press freedom award winner.

text.p: Zambia on Thursday attacked the winner of a prestigious press freedom award for his comments about the Zambian government during a speech this week to the Commonwealth Press Union (CPU) conference in Cape Town.

Fred Mmembe, editor-in-chief of Zambia's independent The Post newspaper, had accused his government of nepotism and undemocratic practices during his acceptance of the CPU Lady Astor Award for press freedom on Monday.
The Zambian government on Thursday released a statement to the CPU conference attacking Mmembe's speech.
"Some Zambian journalists want to turn press freedom into anarchy of the press," it said.
"There is very clear evidence to suggest that The Post is a partisan organisation presently in cahoots with one of the opposition parties," it added.
The CPU is holding an international conference attended by senior media personalities and government officials.

Mmembe currently faces a 25-year jail term in Zambia for contravening the country's State Secrets Act. His paper published a report saying the government was considering a referendum on the country's constitution.
He is due to appear in court next Tuesday. Mmembe told a news conference that he did not know what awaited him in Zambia when he returns on Sunday.
"I have information that when I arrive at the airport I will be thoroughly searched and arrested," he said.
"I am not scared of jail, I have been there before."
In February Mmembe and two colleagues were detained for 24 days for questioning comments by a senior government official.
The Post is Zambia's only independent newspaper and is highly critical of President Frederick Chiluba's government.
The Zambian statement also accused The Post of advocating violence and said there was no harassment of journalists in the country.
CPU spokesman Michael Stent said his organisation would try all in its power to prevent any harm coming to Mmembe.
"We will attempt for him to safely get into Zambia and make sure that he is at all times protected," Stent said.
Stent said the CPU would also write Chiluba a letter.
